## Motivation

`sglang.bench_serving --header` passes custom HTTP headers for authenticated/proxied endpoints, but several server-bound requests used `get_auth_headers()` directly and silently dropped those custom headers:

- the readiness poll (`wait_for_endpoint`)
- the cache flush (`flush_server_cache`)
- the two `/server_info` queries inside `benchmark()`
- model discovery (`/v1/models`) and tokenizer lookup (`/model_info`) in `run_benchmark()`

Only the benchmark's async request paths respected `--header`.

## Modifications

- Folded the auth logic from `get_auth_headers()` into `get_request_headers()` so there is a single request-headers builder that always applies `parse_custom_headers()` (the `--header` flag). This removes the historical `get_auth_headers()` helper, which was the pre-`--header`-era function and had  no remaining call sites that wanted auth *without* the custom headers.
- Switched the 6 call sites above from `get_auth_headers()` to `get_request_headers()`.
- Updated `test_embedding_cache_flush_uses_the_engine_specific_endpoint` to patch `get_request_headers` instead of the removed `get_auth_headers`.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — benchmark tooling change, no model-output impact.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — benchmark tooling change, no inference-path impact.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(not needed — no CLI/doc surface changed)*
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). *(N/A — tooling only)*
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
